title: Vibe Engineering Effect Apps — Michael Arnaldi, Effectful
talk_summary: Michael Arnaldi live-builds an Effect app from an empty repo using a coding agent, arguing the key move is to vendor the library source into the repo (git subtree) so the model can mine patterns from real code rather than docs or MCP. He layers back-pressure on top: strict compiler diagnostics, custom lint rules that ban the shortcuts the model takes, and small persisted 'pattern' markdown files that are generated per-feature and referenced from AGENTS.md.

takeaways.technique: Vendor dependency source into the repo as a subtree
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of relying on node_modules, .gitignore'd dirs, docs or MCP servers, they git-subtree the library source into a visible folder (repos/effect) so the coding agent treats it as first-party code and mines patterns from it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the only way I found the models to be good regardless of the language... is if you just clone the [ __ ] repo

takeaways.technique: Per-feature 'pattern' files generated from source, indexed in AGENTS.md
takeaways.what_they_do: Before implementing a feature, the agent explores the vendored repo and writes a small patterns/<topic>.md (e.g. http-api.md, sql.md, testing.md); AGENTS.md lists the patterns dir so later sessions load only the relevant ones. This self-selects which parts of a big library to adopt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Save your research into patterns http api.md

takeaways.technique: Lint rules as back-pressure against model shortcuts
takeaways.what_they_do: They watch what the model does wrong and encode each failure as an ESLint rule (ban `as` casts, ban `any`/`unknown`, ban SQL-typed interfaces, force branded IDs and schema-level validation at the edge) so the compiler/linter rejects the shortcut before review.

takeaways.technique: Escalate all diagnostics to errors for AI-authored code
takeaways.what_they_do: They configure the type checker so every diagnostic severity (suggestion/warning) becomes an error, on the premise that the model must not be able to land code with any hint of a problem.

takeaways.technique: Fresh context per small task via a loop script
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than one long session, they persist a spec/plan to markdown, then run a simple bash loop that tells the model to pick up one small task, implement it, and exit — restarting the agent to keep the context window clean.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I use a very simple bash script that tells the model pick up a small task implement the small task and then exit and I run that in a loop

takeaways.technique: Model-specific prompt phrasing (don't shout at GPT)
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep AGENTS.md terse and avoid uppercase/aggressive phrasing for GPT-family models because it makes them passive and agreeable, while noting Claude responds to emphatic instructions; they suggest generating patterns per model family.
